claims.text: The protective coating is a multiphase FCC/BCC high-entropy alloy.
The initial coating has a uniform, low-defect microstructure with minimal pre-existing nano-twins.
Sustained elevated loading nucleates nano-twins at or near grain boundaries.
Nano-twins arrest continuity of dislocation slip.
Arresting dislocation-slip continuity limits shear-band propagation.
Limiting shear-band propagation reduces the creep rate under sustained load.
Alloying additions can be selected to inhibit nano-twin formation.
Nano-twins form at slip-band intersections and grain boundaries.
Non-Schmid effects in BCC regions can promote continuity of slip across grain boundaries.
Under deformation, slip bands can transmit continuously across grain boundaries and subsequently develop localized strain and shear bands.
Load-induced nano-twins act as barriers to dislocation transmission across grain boundaries.
Twin-mediated interruption of dislocation transmission delays strain localization and shear-band development.
Samples that readily form nano-twins will have lower creep rates than samples in which nano-twin formation is chemically suppressed.
Samples that readily form nano-twins will exhibit less shear-band propagation than samples in which nano-twin formation is chemically suppressed.
The proposed mechanism operates under sustained stress at temperatures that promote dislocation activity.
At sufficiently high stress or temperature, alternative deformation modes such as diffusion creep may diminish the protective effect of nano-twinning.
Suppressing nano-twin formation should produce significantly higher creep rates or more pronounced shear bands if nano-twinning governs creep resistance.
